item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong indirect evidence of patronage and politicized state power, but no clean, direct 2024 example of a national welfare/permits/jobs/food/housing program explicitly being used as a loyalty-and-punishment mechanism. The positive evidence is mostly needs-based humanitarian delivery or safety-net modernization, much of it partner-led. So the best-supported conclusion is: Hasina’s 2024 record does not show clear avoidance of patronage politics, and the broader state context points the other way.","evidence":[{"title":"Bangladesh - Cash Transfer Modernization Project: Improving Transparency and Efficiency of Safety Nets","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-01-01","url":"https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099739201032424234","summary":"Bangladesh already had cash-transfer programs aimed at the poorest and most socially excluded, including widows and older people, and the project aimed to modernize delivery and improve transparency. This is limited positive evidence against loyalty-based distribution, but it does not show the system was fully depoliticized.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.4","6B.2","6B.3"]},{"title":"UN and partners seek $852.4M to support Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi hosts","publisher":"UNHCR / UN in Bangladesh","date":"2024-03-13","url":"https://www.unhcr.org/news/press-releases/un-and-partners-seek-852-4m-support-rohingya-refugees-and-bangladeshi-hosts","summary":"The response plan targeted food, shelter, health care, protection, education, and livelihood support for Rohingya refugees and host communities, especially women and children. This is needs-based allocation, not obvious loyalty punishment, but it is partner-led humanitarian delivery rather than proof of Hasina’s own restraint.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.6","6B.2","6B.3"]},{"title":"UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024","publisher":"UNFPA Bangladesh","date":"2024","url":"https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024","summary":"UNFPA reported targeted services for women, girls, adolescents, persons with disabilities, and disaster-affected areas, including emergency reproductive health, GBV services, and cash assistance. This is the strongest positive item on 6B.7, but it still looks humanitarian and externally financed rather than evidence that Hasina broadly rejected patronage politics.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.6","6B.2","6B.3"]},{"title":"Freedom in the World 2024: Bangladesh","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House said corruption was endemic, anticorruption enforcement was politicized, ruling-party control over state resources created coercive economic power, and minorities and refugees, especially Rohingya, faced discrimination and restricted access to health care and education. This does not prove welfare goods were used as rewards, but it strongly supports a broader pattern of coercive political control rather than neutral, rights-respecting access to state benefits.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.4","6B.5","6B.2"]}]}
